supportingConnections.hypothesis: With hundreds of ideas, search is the only way humans and agents find existing work before duplicating it.
Duration and variance make the priority honest about time and uncertainty, so ranking favors work that pays off soon and reliably.
Smaller stores let agents change one concern without reading 2500 lines, which cuts regressions and context cost.
A smaller App.vue keeps layout changes local and reviewable.
Tests written first give autonomous agents a definition of done that does not depend on a human checking each change.
One router per domain lets features grow without one server file becoming the bottleneck for every change.
Spinning a branch off into its own repo lets a sub-project grow its own community without dragging the whole graph along.
Archiving that keeps settled ideas out of the way keeps the working graph small enough to read.
